plan: Economic theory suggests bidding one's true value is optimal in a second-price sealed bid auction. My value is $49, which is the highest possible. Since the dominant strategy is to bid my true value, and there's no previous round history to suggest a different approach, I will bid exactly $49. This maximizes my potential profit by ensuring I win if anyone else bids below my value, and I'll only pay the second-highest bid.

Economic theory suggests the dominant strategy is to bid my true value of $44. This is because:
1. If I bid less, I risk losing the item even when winning would be profitable
2. If I bid more, I risk paying more than the item is worth to me
3. With values drawn independently each round, past strategies don't apply
4. Second-price auction mechanics incentivize honest bidding
Therefore, I will bid my exact value of $44.

Economic theory suggests the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my private value of $22. In a single-round sealed bid auction with independent value draws, bidding my true value minimizes the risk of either overbidding (losing money) or underbidding (missing a potential win. Since values are randomly drawn and this is a one-time game, strategic complexity is reduced to simply revealing my true valuation.
